title: As he speaks, he does
hook: the Tathagata does as he says and says as he does (Itivuttaka 112)
carry: as he speaks, so he does

segments.voice: Yesterday: walking, standing, sitting, lying down. Your line: effort is alive. Today, the last discourse of the Itivuttaka, and a name explained.

A coach yells at players to stay calm, red in the face. A parent says put the phone away, while scrolling. A friend swears they'll be on time, again. The gap between saying and doing is easy to spot, usually faster in other people than in ourselves. The Itivuttaka's very last discourse names one person in whom, it says, the gap isn't there at all, and it builds one of his titles out of that.
screen: `CALM DOWN, SHOUTED.` → `THE GAP BETWEEN SAYING AND DOING.` → `THE LAST DISCOURSE.`

segments.voice: Itivuttaka 112 lists reasons the Buddha is called Tathagata, a title he uses for himself in the suttas. Tradition reads the word as thus-gone or thus-come, and the discourse plays with it. He has fully understood the world, its arising, its ending, and the way to its ending. From the night of his awakening to the night of his final passing, whatever he says is so and not otherwise. And then the line for today. In Pali it has a lovely rhythm: yathavadi tathakari, yathakari tathavadi. As he says, so he does. As he does, so he says. It runs both directions. Plenty of people do what they say, eventually. Fewer say only what they actually do: no padding, no spin, no talking themselves up. The sutta wants both. That's why, it says, he is called Tathagata, the one who is thus. There's a practical side to this for anyone who isn't a Buddha. Elsewhere the texts tell of the Buddha's teaching to his son Rahula: before you act, while you act, after you act, look at it. Does it match? A life where words and deeds line up has one big advantage: there's nothing to keep track of. No cover stories, no two versions. And it's the end of a collection whose every discourse began, this was said by the Blessed One. It closes with a picture of someone whose saying and doing are the same thing.
screen: `WHY HE IS CALLED TATHAGATA` · `WHATEVER HE SAYS IS SO` · `AS HE SAYS, SO HE DOES, AND BACK` · `NOTHING TO KEEP TRACK OF` · then, large: `AS HE SPEAKS, SO HE DOES.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one thing you've said lately that you meant, I'll call, I'll help, I'll rest more, and hold it lightly. Picture the deed that would match it, as small and specific as you can, the call at six, the phone left in the other room, and see yourself doing it. Let the word and the deed sit side by side until they feel like one thing.
Yathavadi tathakari. As he says, so he does, and as he does, so he says: Itivuttaka 112's reason the Buddha is called Tathagata. Today's word.
Your line: as he speaks, so he does. Word and deed, running both directions. Six hundred thirty-four days on the path.

howItsDone: Buddhists in many traditions take the Buddha's consistency of word and deed as a model; monastics in many places recite the rules of training together regularly, partly so that what they say they keep is matched by what they do.

fork.setup: you've promised to help a friend move on Saturday. a better plan comes up. what does as he speaks, so he does point to?
options: keep the promise, or tell the friend honestly and early.
go to the better plan and explain later.
say yes to both and hope it works out.
fork.reveal: the discourse asks for word and deed to match in both directions: do what you said, and say only what you'll actually do.

original.note: Pali: as he says, so he does. the reason given in Itivuttaka 112 for the title Tathagata.

trapdoor: what you thought: as he speaks, he does is a saying about keeping promises.
what it means: in Itivuttaka 112, one of the reasons the Buddha is called Tathagata: his words and deeds match in both directions.
what a scholar hears: the same passage appears in the Anguttara Nikaya's fours; the play on tatha, thus, in yathavadi tathakari is part of the old explanations of the word Tathagata.

chat.says: Why does the Itivuttaka's last teaching call the Buddha Tathagata?
options: One reason: as he says, so he does, and as he does, so he says.
Because he never spoke at all, and taught only by his silent example.
Because he was born into a royal family of that name in the north.
chat.meaning: Itivuttaka 112: as he says, so he does; as he does, so he says. That's one reason it gives for the title Tathagata.
